PAPERS.journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
PAPERS.title: Rural outdoor air pollution exceeds urban levels in the Delhi megacity region.
PAPERS.short: 49-site calibrated lower-cost PM2.5 network across a 160 km Delhi urbanicity transect: rural PM2.5 exceeds urban by ~20% in every month (Jul-Nov 2024); rural morning/evening solid-fuel peaks missed by satellite products
PAPERS.pm: Hourly PM2.5 from a calibrated lower-cost sensor network (49 sites, 300-30,000 people/km2), 160 km transect plus stratified village, small-city and Delhi sites
PAPERS.endpoint: Rural-urban PM2.5 gradient and diurnal structure
PAPERS.n: Five months (July-November 2024) of a 49-site lower-cost PM2.5 network spanning population densities of 300 to 30,000 people/km2 inside and outside Delhi, including a 160 km transect. Rural sites exceeded urban sites by about 20% in every month, from the monsoon minimum to the post-monsoon maximum. Rural diurnal cycles carried sharp 06:00-10:00 and 16:00-20:00 LT peaks absent at urban sites, attributed to solid-fuel cooking, heating and small industry. Satellite-derived PM2.5 did not reproduce the rural enhancement. Weakness: calibration procedure, reference co-location and humidity correction are not described in the abstract, and a 20% gradient is within the range a site-specific RH or aerosol-composition bias can generate if rural and urban sensors were corrected with one model. Relevance: direct - a network result that overturns the urban-hotspot assumption and documents a satellite blind spot that only ground sensors can see.

PAPERS.title: Association of ambient particulate matter and neighborhood walkability with risk of asthma in Ningbo, China.
PAPERS.short: Yinzhou cohort, 26,926 adults, 1,032 incident asthma: PM1/PM2.5/PM10 and nitrate/ammonium/sulfate HR 1.09-1.30 per IQR; PM1 up + walkability down joint HR 1.39 (1.22-1.58), additive interaction
PAPERS.pm: Long-term residential PM1, PM2.5, PM10 and PM2.5 nitrate, ammonium and sulfate from satellite-derived products; Walk Score walkability
PAPERS.n: 26,926 adults of the Yinzhou Cohort followed 152,748 person-years; 1,032 incident asthma cases from the regional health information system. In single-exposure Cox models, PM1, PM2.5, PM10 and the nitrate, ammonium and sulfate components gave HRs per IQR from 1.09 (95% CI 1.00-1.20) to 1.30 (1.19-1.43); the abstract does not attribute each HR to a pollutant. An IQR rise in walkability gave HR 0.89 (0.82-0.96). Associations attenuated in two-exposure models. An IQR increase in PM1 combined with an IQR decrease in walkability gave a joint HR of 1.39 (1.22-1.58), with additive interaction. Weakness: walkability and satellite PM are both urban-form surrogates and share confounding by traffic and socioeconomic position; registry-based asthma onset is prone to ascertainment differences by healthcare access. Relevance: PM1 carries the interaction signal, a fraction optical low-cost sensors report but satellites estimate least well.

PAPERS.title: Ambient air pollution exposure before and during pregnancy and risk of hypertensive disorders of pregnancy: A large cohort study in Sichuan, China.
PAPERS.short: 1,330,109 singleton pregnancies, Sichuan 2013-2022: six-pollutant mixture OR 1.53 (1.46-1.60) for HDP in the 13 pre-pregnancy weeks; DLNM places PM2.5 associations in pre-pregnancy and early gestation
PAPERS.pm: Residential O3, SO2, NO2, CO, PM2.5 and PM10 from gridded pollution data at geocoded addresses, 13 weeks before conception to gestational week 20; quantile g-computation and DLNM
PAPERS.n: Multicentre retrospective cohort of 1,330,109 singleton pregnancies (2013-2022) with gridded exposures from 13 weeks before pregnancy to gestational week 20. Ozone per IQR: OR 1.36 (1.29-1.42) pre-pregnancy and 1.30 (1.26-1.34) in weeks 1-4. The six-pollutant mixture by quantile g-computation: OR 1.53 (1.46-1.60) pre-pregnancy and 1.25 (1.21-1.30) in weeks 1-4. DLNMs showed pre-pregnancy weekly associations for all six pollutants and early-gestation associations for O3, SO2 and PM2.5; no PM-specific estimate is given in the abstract, so nothing is plotted. Weakness: the gridded product is unnamed, residence is fixed across a window that starts before conception, and HDP ascertainment from hospital records varies by centre. Relevance: pre-conception windows are where residential mobility and model error dominate - personal or home monitoring would bound both.

PAPERS.title: Preconceptional parental air pollution exposure and clinical pregnancy after assisted conception: Identifying parent-specific vulnerability windows and high-risk subpopulations.
PAPERS.short: 19,358 assisted-conception cycles, 9,943 couples, Shandong: parental PM2.5, PM10, NO2, SO2 raise clinical-pregnancy failure; NO2 strongest (aOR 1.41 per 10 ug/m3); maternal days 180-86, paternal days 69-15 sensitive
PAPERS.pm: Daily maternal and paternal PM2.5, PM10, NO2, SO2 and O3 at 1-km resolution during gametogenesis windows
PAPERS.endpoint: Clinical pregnancy failure after assisted conception
PAPERS.n: 19,358 assisted-conception cycles from 9,943 couples (2014-2024) with 1-km daily exposure for each parent across gametogenesis; multilevel logistic models. Parental PM2.5, PM10, NO2 and SO2 were each associated with clinical-pregnancy failure; NO2 was strongest (maternal aOR 1.410, 95% CI 1.339-1.486 per 10 ug/m3) and O3 was inverse. PM-specific estimates are not in the abstract. Sensitive windows: maternal days 180-86 (preantral follicle) and paternal days 69-15 (late spermatogenesis) before treatment; susceptibility higher with IVF/ICSI, secondary infertility and age 35 or over. Weakness: the inverse O3 association signals residual seasonal confounding of treatment timing, and couples share a residence, so maternal and paternal windows are separated by timing, not by independent exposure. Relevance: low-moderate - window-specific claims at 1 km rest on daily model accuracy that dense networks could test.

PAPERS.title: Multidimensional Evaluation of Heavy Metal Exposure and Biochemical Alterations in Occupationally Exposed Foundry Workers.
PAPERS.short: 320 foundry workers, 200 personal samples (NIOSH 7300, ICP-OES): Fe, Mn, Pb, Cd, Cu often above OELs; Pb/Cd/Cr/Ni inversely related to FEV1/FVC; As ELCR 4.1e-4
PAPERS.pm: Airborne metal concentrations from 200 personal breathing-zone samples (NIOSH 7300, ICP-OES) across eight work units
PAPERS.endpoint: Spirometry, liver and kidney markers, lipids, haematology; inhalation HQ/HI and ELCR
PAPERS.n: Cross-sectional study of 320 workers across eight units of a metal-casting plant; 200 personal air samples analysed for metals by ICP-OES. Fe, Mn, Pb, Cd and Cu frequently exceeded occupational limits, highest in smelting/rolling and casting. Pb, Cd, Cr and Ni were inversely associated with FEV1 and FVC; ALT and AST were higher in the high-exposure group. HQ exceeded 1 for Fe, Mn, Cr, Cd and Pb in the high group; ELCR exceeded 1e-4 for As, Pb, Cd, Cr and Ni, As highest at 4.1e-4. No effect sizes per unit exposure in the abstract. Weakness: unit membership is the de facto exposure, so co-exposures (heat, silica, smoking) and healthy-worker selection go uncontrolled; particle size fraction is not reported. Relevance: low - metal-rich workplace aerosol is the case where mass-only optical sensors understate hazard.

PAPERS.title: 7,8-Dihydroxyflavone attenuates PM(2.5)-induced oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction and apoptosis in human HaCaT keratinocytes.
PAPERS.short: HaCaT keratinocytes: 7,8-dihydroxyflavone blunts PM2.5-induced ROS, lipid peroxidation, mitochondrial depolarisation and JNK-dependent apoptosis
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5 suspension applied to HaCaT keratinocytes (source, dose and composition not given in abstract)
PAPERS.endpoint: Keratinocyte oxidative stress, mitochondrial function and apoptosis
PAPERS.n: In vitro study in human HaCaT keratinocytes. PM2.5 raised intracellular ROS, lipid peroxidation and calcium, reduced mitochondrial membrane potential and ATP, and triggered cytochrome c release, caspase activation and apoptosis; 7,8-dihydroxyflavone pretreatment reversed these changes. JNK inhibition (SP600125) and JNK1/2 siRNA reduced PM2.5-induced cytotoxicity, implicating JNK signalling. Weakness: particle source, dose in ug/cm2 and composition are not given in the abstract, so dosimetric relevance to skin deposition cannot be judged; a single immortalised line with a single protectant. Relevance: low - mechanistic support for dermal PM effects, no exposure-measurement content.

PAPERS.title: An Exploratory Comparison of Indoor Air Quality and Culturable Airborne Microbial Concentrations Among Hospital Waiting Areas With Different Ventilation Conditions in Northern Thailand.
PAPERS.short: Five hospital waiting areas, northern Thailand, nine days: PM10, temperature and culturable bacteria/fungi differ by area; no pairwise difference survives Holm; PM10 does not predict bioaerosol counts
PAPERS.pm: Indoor PM2.5, PM10, CO2, CO, temperature and RH (instruments not specified in abstract) with culturable bacterial and fungal sampling, summarised by room-day
PAPERS.endpoint: Indoor air quality and culturable bioaerosol by ventilation type
PAPERS.n: Exploratory monitoring of five hospital waiting areas (one mechanically ventilated) over nine sampling days, summarised at room-day level. Overall differences were significant for PM10 (p=0.0012), temperature, culturable bacteria and fungi, but not PM2.5, RH, CO or CO2; no pairwise contrast survived Holm adjustment. The mechanically ventilated room tended to have lower PM10 and bioaerosol. Mixed-effects and fixed-effects models found no association between PM10 and culturable bacteria or fungi (p 0.06-0.54). Weakness: ventilation type is confounded with room (n=1 mechanically ventilated) and the PM instrument and its calibration are not reported. Relevance: low - illustrates that indoor PM mass is not a proxy for viable bioaerosol, a limit on what PM sensors can stand in for in clinical spaces.

PAPERS.title: Air quality benefits and carbon reduction potential of future ultra-low emission retrofits in the chinese coking industry.
PAPERS.short: Plant-level 2023 inventory of China coking: 16.0 kt PM, 88.2 kt NOx, 129.3 kt VOC, 227.8 Mt CO2; synergistic retrofit cuts PM 43% and the sector PM2.5 contribution 53.5%
PAPERS.pm: Plant- and process-level PM, SO2, NOx, VOC and CO2 emission inventory for 2023 with air-quality simulations of sector contributions to ambient PM2.5
PAPERS.endpoint: Sector emissions and contribution to ambient PM2.5 under ultra-low-emission scenarios
PAPERS.n: Nationwide plant- and process-level inventory of China's coking industry for 2023. Compliance with PM and SO2 concentration limits exceeded 99.6% at all stages; NOx compliance at the coke-oven stack was 86.5%. Sector emissions: PM 16.01, SO2 26.55, NOx 88.16 and VOCs 129.33 kt/yr, CO2 227.80 Mt/yr. Under a synergistic pollutant-CO2 scenario, PM falls 43.3%, VOCs 77.9% and CO2 54.7%; modelled sector contributions to ambient PM2.5, SO2, NO2 and O3 fall 53.5%, 20.7%, 40.0% and 15.8%. Weakness: compliance rates come from reported stack concentrations, which may overstate real-world performance, and the absolute ambient PM2.5 change is not given. Relevance: low-moderate - sets source expectations against which fence-line sensor networks near coking clusters could be checked.

PAPERS.title: Bicycle-Based Multipollutant Monitoring in an Urban Industrial Area: A Case Study of Background Variability and Local Air Pollution Contrasts
PAPERS.short: Eleven bicycle surveys, 11 km Incheon route: pseudo-wavelet baseline puts 80-84% of PM2.5 in background under westerlies vs 54-68% under easterlies; industrial TVOC 6.5-7.8x residential
PAPERS.pm: Bicycle-borne PM2.5, PM10, equivalent black carbon and PID TVOC on a 50 m grid; pseudo-wavelet background separation; compared with hourly regulatory stations
PAPERS.endpoint: Background vs local fractions of PM2.5, PM10, eBC and TVOC by microenvironment and wind sector
PAPERS.n: Eleven bicycle surveys on an ~11 km route through four microenvironments (September-November 2025) measured PM2.5, PM10, eBC and a PID TVOC signal; a pseudo-wavelet baseline, tested on synthetic plume and trend cases, split background from local enhancement. Background share of PM2.5 was 80.4-84.3% under westerly winds and 54.0-68.4% under easterlies; local fractions were consistently larger for PM10 than PM2.5. Industrial-zone local TVOC was 6.5-7.8 times residential; eBC enhancements followed roads. The estimated PM background tracked nearby roadside and urban monitors closely, port and national-background stations less so. Weakness: eleven runs cannot separate wind regime from season or weekday, and instrument types and their humidity handling are not stated. Relevance: direct - a reusable background-subtraction method for mobile and low-cost survey data.

PAPERS.title: Tropical cyclone amplifies anthropogenic influences on aerosol-cloud interactions over the South China Sea
PAPERS.short: Shipborne AMS over the South China Sea: Typhoon Chaba switches air to Indochina outflow, NR-PM1 rises, OA share 14.6% to 44.9%, kappa falls ~60%, CCN up to sixfold, droplet radius 11-37% smaller
PAPERS.pm: Shipborne non-refractory PM1 composition (aerosol mass spectrometry), hygroscopicity (kappa) and CCN, 22 June-5 July 2022
PAPERS.endpoint: Aerosol composition, hygroscopicity, CCN and cloud microphysics under tropical-cyclone transport
PAPERS.n: Shipborne measurements over the South China Sea (22 June-5 July 2022) around Typhoon Chaba. The cyclone circulation shifted air from local marine to long-range Indochina transport, raising NR-PM1; organic aerosol rose from 14.6% to 44.9% of NR-PM1, mainly oxygenated OA from transport plus local heterogeneous oxidation. Bulk hygroscopicity kappa fell about 60% while kappa of OA rose about 27%; CCN increased up to sixfold. Parcel modelling with observations gave 11-37% smaller droplet effective radius and 6-26% larger autoconversion radius, confirmed by satellite. Weakness: a single two-week cruise and one cyclone; transport and in-situ oxidation are inferred from correlations with Ox and RH. Relevance: indirect - a 60% swing in kappa within days is the size of composition-driven hygroscopic change that breaks fixed humidity corrections for optical PM sensors.

PAPERS.title: Technical note: Deep-GF-PRM – a deep learning framework for parameterizing aerosol hygroscopic growth factor probability density function
PAPERS.short: Deep-GF-PRM: physics-embedded neural network maps HTDMA responses directly to growth-factor PDF modal parameters; reproduces synthetic PDFs and matches nonparametric inversion on field data
PAPERS.pm: Humidified tandem DMA instrument responses; growth-factor probability density functions of atmospheric aerosol
PAPERS.endpoint: Retrieval accuracy of hygroscopic growth-factor PDF modal parameters
PAPERS.n: Technical note. A deep neural network embedding the HTDMA kernel function and physical constraints maps instrument responses directly to the modal parameters of the hygroscopic growth-factor PDF, replacing inversion followed by Gaussian fitting. Trained on synthetic responses spanning many GF-PDFs and noise levels, it reproduced synthetic PDFs with high fidelity, and on real measurements agreed closely with nonparametric inversion. No numerical error metrics in the abstract. Weakness: validation against nonparametric inversion tests consistency with an existing method, not truth, and performance outside the synthetic training envelope (e.g. multimodal externally mixed aerosol) is unreported. Relevance: indirect - faster, standardised growth-factor retrieval feeds the kappa inputs that physically based humidity corrections for low-cost optical sensors need.

PAPERS.title: Indoor Exposure to Wildfire Smoke: A Critical Review of Infiltration, Assessment, and Removal
PAPERS.short: Critical review of indoor wildfire-smoke PM2.5: falling I/O ratio is not proof of intervention effect; portable-filtration effect sizes depend on design; calls for synchronised indoor-outdoor and personal measurement
PAPERS.pm: Indoor and outdoor PM2.5 during wildfire smoke from field measurements, sensor networks, intervention studies and building models
PAPERS.endpoint: Infiltration, assessment and removal of wildfire-smoke PM2.5 indoors
PAPERS.n: Critical review of field measurements, intervention studies and building models of wildfire smoke indoors, focused on interpreting indoor PM2.5. Indoor concentrations below outdoor can still be substantial exposure, and a lower indoor/outdoor ratio alone does not demonstrate intervention effect. Sensor networks show large between-building variation; portable filtration reduces particles, but short room tests, sequential household and concurrent controlled designs estimate different effects. Higher outdoor concentrations raise residual indoor PM without necessarily lowering fractional filtration effectiveness. Gas-phase and semi-volatile evidence is thin. Weakness: no systematic search or pooling is described, so coverage is the authors' selection. Relevance: direct - names synchronised indoor-outdoor and personal measurement, the low-cost-sensor use case, as the missing evidence.

PAPERS.title: Effect of Filter Characteristics on Particulate Matter Reduction in Residential Ventilation Systems
PAPERS.short: Residential mechanical ventilation with SMPS-verified artificial PM2.5: 30T HEPA reaches 94.4-98.8% removal; replacement interval ~526 days (395-789) as an upper bound
PAPERS.pm: Artificially generated PM2.5 verified by SMPS; whole-unit removal by filter type and thickness, with accelerated ageing
PAPERS.endpoint: Whole-system PM2.5 removal efficiency, reduction time and filter service life
PAPERS.n: Laboratory tests of whole residential ventilation units rather than filters alone, using dust-collection filters of several types and thicknesses challenged with artificial PM2.5 whose size distribution was verified by SMPS. A reduction-time model predicts the time to remove PM2.5 given indoor generation. A 30T HEPA filter achieved 94.4-98.8% PM2.5 mass removal; accelerated ageing gave an estimated replacement interval of about 526 days (395-789) under the 2024 ambient PM2.5 distribution, stated as an upper bound. Weakness: artificial aerosol and laboratory conditions omit real infiltration, occupant sources and humidity loading of filters. Relevance: moderate - ventilation-unit performance is what in-home low-cost sensors are increasingly used to verify in the field.

PAPERS.title: Air Pollution Research in Latin America and the Caribbean, 2015–2025: Growth, Gaps, and Future Challenges
PAPERS.short: Latin America and Caribbean air-pollution literature 2015-2025, 6,355 papers: attention scales sublinearly with burden (slope 0.72, 0.52-0.91); under-represented countries carry 30% of burden with 5% of attention
PAPERS.pm: Bibliometric mapping of PM2.5-centred air-pollution research; burden compared with research attention by country
PAPERS.endpoint: Research attention vs burden, themes and collaboration structure
PAPERS.n: Systematic Scopus and Web of Science search with regex plus LLM screening (94% agreement with author labels; ~80.5% relevance among retained records) yielding 6,355 LAC air-pollution publications, 2015-2025. Annual publications rose 83% (389 to 713); five countries held 82.7% of country mentions. Research attention tracked burden sublinearly (log-log slope 0.72, 95% CI 0.52-0.91, R2 0.64); under-represented countries carried 30% of burden but 5% of attention. Five themes centred on PM2.5 and health. Intra-LAC collaboration (9.4%) was about four times rarer than partnership with external, mostly high-income, institutions (38.0%). Weakness: LLM screening with ~20% irrelevant retained records and Scopus/WoS coverage that under-indexes Spanish- and Portuguese-language venues. Relevance: identifies where low-cost networks would add the most evidence per dollar.

PAPERS.title: Impact of crop-residue burning timing on PM2.5 pollution and population exposure in Northeast China: Insights from Himawari-constrained CMAQ simulations
PAPERS.short: Crop-residue burning timing, PM2.5 and population exposure in Northeast China from Himawari-constrained CMAQ (per title)
PAPERS.design: Metadata only: no abstract in Crossref at issue time
PAPERS.pm: Not stated (title names Himawari-constrained CMAQ simulations of PM2.5)
PAPERS.endpoint: PM2.5 and population exposure by timing of crop-residue burning (per title)
PAPERS.n: Metadata only: no abstract was retrievable from the harvest legs or Crossref at issue time. The record (Atmospheric Environment; Yang, Chen, Li, Li) uses Himawari-constrained CMAQ simulations to relate the timing of crop-residue burning to PM2.5 and population exposure in Northeast China. No finding, emission estimate or exposure figure is asserted here. Relevance: moderate - geostationary fire constraints on a CTM are the satellite half of the satellite-surface fusion problem; seasonal burning is where sparse regulatory networks miss rural peaks.

PAPERS.title: Wintertime black carbon variability and potential source regions over Aizawl, Northeast India
PAPERS.short: Wintertime black-carbon variability and potential source regions at Aizawl, Northeast India (per title)
PAPERS.design: Metadata only: no abstract in Crossref at issue time
PAPERS.pm: Black carbon (title); instrument and period not available
PAPERS.endpoint: Black-carbon variability and source regions (per title)
PAPERS.n: Metadata only: no abstract was retrievable from the harvest legs or Crossref at issue time. The record (Science of The Total Environment; Gurung, Hazarika, Ranjan, Gupta) reports wintertime black-carbon variability and potential source regions over Aizawl in Northeast India. No concentration, source apportionment or instrument is asserted here. Relevance: low-moderate - an under-monitored hill region where BC is likely transported from biomass burning upwind.

PAPERS.title: Characterization of New Particle Formation and Emission Flux from a Composting Site
PAPERS.short: New particle formation and particle emission flux from a composting site (per title)
PAPERS.design: Metadata only: no abstract in Crossref at issue time
PAPERS.pm: Particle number / new particle formation (title); instrument not available
PAPERS.endpoint: New particle formation and emission flux (per title)
PAPERS.n: Metadata only: no abstract was retrievable from the harvest legs or Crossref at issue time. The record (Atmospheric Environment; Han, Cai, Ivanova, Meskhidze) characterises new particle formation and particle emission flux at a composting site. No finding or flux value is asserted here. Relevance: low-moderate - composting is an unregistered ultrafine source that mass-based optical sensors would not register.

PAPERS.title: Bidimensional charge distribution of spherical and aggregate nanoparticles in a unipolar diffusion charger
PAPERS.short: Bidimensional charge distribution of spherical and aggregate nanoparticles in a unipolar diffusion charger (per title)
PAPERS.design: Metadata only: no abstract in Crossref at issue time
PAPERS.pm: Nanoparticle charging in a unipolar diffusion charger (title)
PAPERS.endpoint: Charge distribution vs particle morphology (per title)
PAPERS.n: Metadata only: no abstract was retrievable from the harvest legs or Crossref at issue time. The record (Journal of Aerosol Science; Sapkota, Mehri, Corbin, Rogak) addresses the two-dimensional charge distribution of spherical and aggregate nanoparticles in a unipolar diffusion charger. No result is asserted here. Relevance: moderate - unipolar diffusion charging underlies compact electrical ultrafine and lung-deposited-surface-area sensors, whose response to soot aggregates depends on exactly this morphology dependence.

PAPERS.n: Metadata only: no abstract was retrievable from the harvest legs or Crossref at issue time.
